scope: 768d hnswlib and FAISS-HNSW: all stored per-query results; not a performance benchmark
algorithm: Sort each returned top-10 and GT top-10, then use a scalar two-pointer merge to count matches; compare each stored hit and aggregate recall.
independence: Standalone script does not import benchmark runner or reviewer; its scalar sorted-merge algorithm differs from the sampler set intersection and supervisor NumPy broadcasting. NumPy is shared only for reading NPZ and memory-mapping int32 GT.
limitations: GT is the same dataset ground truth, not a newly computed exact-search oracle.
TriviumDB original benchmark does not retain per-query IDs; it is outside this audit.
Boundary hashes do not exclude data modified and restored between snapshots.
Passing recall checks does not waive any QPS stability or product test failure.
